title: AI-based Anesthesia Risk Identification and Stratification for the Elderly - Usability Study
summary:
Before surgery, it is important to assess patients' health status and potential risks as accurately as possible. This can be particularly challenging in older patients due to multiple medical conditions, the use of several medications, or physical limitations.

The ARISE-Clinical study investigates how easily older patients can use a newly developed digital application to provide their medical history. A total of 100 patients aged 65 years or older who are scheduled for elective surgery will answer questions about their health using the digital application. The collected information will subsequently be structured and processed using artificial intelligence (AI), with the aim of potentially supporting preoperative medical risk assessment in the future.

After using the application, participants will evaluate its usability through standardized questionnaires. The study will also assess the technical reliability of the application and identify potential difficulties during its use.

Routine medical care will remain unchanged. The AI-generated results will not be used for medical decision-making in this study.
conditions: No specific disease is being investigated. The digital application is intended to generate a structured overview based on patient-reported health information to support preoperative risk assessment.

interventions.name: Geriatric patients attending a preoperative anesthesia consultation prior to a surgical procedure use a newly developed digital medical history assessment tool for risk stratification. Subsequently, they complete a one-time questionnaire to evaluate the tool’s usability using the System Usability Sc

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Presentation at the preoperative anesthesia assessment clinic prior to an elective surgical procedure during the recruitment period; ability to use the data collection application independently or with technical assistance; written informed consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of capacity to provide informed consent; linguistic, cognitive, or functional limitations that prevent use of the application even with permissible technical assistance; refusal or withdrawal of informed consent
